newsitem.title: UK: Syria thought to have cancelled sugar tender -trad.
newsitem.headline: Syria thought to have cancelled sugar tender -trad.

text.p: Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) is believed to have cancelled its tender to buy white and raw sugar, European trade sources said on Wednesday.
There was no immediate reason for the cancellation, they said.

GEZA tendered last month to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws. The final date to receive price offers was set as June 17 and shipment periods were between July 15 and August 15.
Traders said offers on the white sugar varied in an approximate range of $369 and $373, with the upper end of the range described as "aggressive".
GEZA has cancelled tenders in the past saying price offers do not match its conditions.
Syria bought a cargo of raws in March at $290 per tonne for April/May shipment but is not believed to have bought white sugar for some time, market sources said.
